data.standardized_narrative: At 31 December 2017 the syndicate's gross claims outstanding comparatives were $682.0m (opening). During 2017 management reported releases of prior year reserves totalling $39.7m, primarily driven by favourable claims development (notably within specialty lines where releases mainly derived from the 2010, 2013, 2014 and 2015 years of account). The second-half 2017 catastrophe activity (hurricanes Harvey, Irma and Maria, Mexican earthquakes and Californian wildfires) increased current-year claims but did not prevent prior year releases overall.

data.data_quality_notes: All monetary amounts are reported in the syndicate's functional currency (USD) though field names reference 'gbp' per schema. The prior year development figure (-39.7) was taken from the explicit narrative statement 'we have been able to release prior year reserves of $39.7m' and is treated as a gross amount. The segmental reserve release table provides division-level gross releases; these were mapped to standard LOBs where best-fit (e.g. 'Political, accident & contingency' -> 'Accident & Health', 'Reinsurance' -> 'Treaty', 'Specialty lines' -> 'Professional Lines'). A gross claims development triangle is present in the technical provisions notes but was not extracted into development_rows due to formatting (aggregate columns and managed-level adjustments); the triangle presence is noted below.

_claims_triangle.notes: A gross claims liabilities table (Beazley managed level and 623 share) and gross ultimate % development tables are present in the Technical Provisions note (page ~46). The detailed development-period rows in monetary amounts were not provided in a simple 'At end of UW year / One year later / Two years later' grid for direct extraction (many tables show percentage development or managed-level aggregates and a 'non-623 share' deduction). Users requiring an analytic triangle should consult the technical provisions pages (gross and net development % tables and the gross claims liabilities by underwriting year) to reconstruct the development diagonals. RITC/managed-level adjustments may distort simple diagonal comparisons.
